resources.string: KeyCatch needs the microphone to hear the music.
KeyCatch can\'t hear without the microphone. Turn it on for KeyCatch in your phone\'s settings.
Hold your phone near the music and tap Listen.
Hold your phone near the singers and tap Listen.
The key, the chord and the tempo show up within a few bars.
The key and how in tune the singers are show up after a line or two. Tap along to set the tempo.

This removes every recorded clip and its notes from the phone. Copies you have already shared are not affected.

A clip keeps up to 60 seconds of microphone audio on this phone, with the time it was made, what KeyCatch heard, and any notes you add. It records everyone nearby, so let the people singing know. Nothing is uploaded. A clip leaves the phone only when you choose Share, and you can delete all clips at any time.
The A your band tunes to. Sharp and flat are measured from it.
Numbers shows each chord by its place in the key, like 1, 4, 5 and 6m (the Nashville system).

In Band and Guitar modes, Accurate hears each note with a small learned model, Basic Pitch. It gets chords and keys right a little more often, even when the band is out of tune. Chords show about a second later, and the phone works harder. If Details says the phone is falling behind, choose Standard.

In Band and Guitar modes, Accurate follows the beat with a learned model (Beat This!). It gets the tempo and the time signature right more often, and the phone works harder. If Details says the phone is falling behind, choose Standard.

Accurate follows the singers with a learned model, CREPE. It finds the right note more often, most of all in a noisy room, and the phone works harder. If Details says the phone is falling behind, choose Standard.
Do Re Mi uses fixed Do, so C is always Do.
Each song is saved here once KeyCatch has found its key and you press New song or Stop. The list stays on this phone.
This removes every saved song from the list. Lists you have already shared are not affected.
KeyCatch listens for the notes and chords and makes its best guess at the key. Usually the guess is right. Here is when it can go wrong.
If people sing between notes, KeyCatch has to guess. You\'ll see \"a guess\" under the key when that happens.
Groups often creep sharp or flat through a long song. KeyCatch follows them, but it can fall behind or settle on the key next door.
A lift for the last chorus takes a few seconds to catch. When a new song starts, press New song so the old one doesn\'t get in the way.
Major or minor isn\'t clear yet.
C major and A minor use the same notes. KeyCatch waits for clues, like where the lines come to rest, so give it a moment.
Talking, clapping, a loud fan or a phone in a pocket can drown out the music. Hold the phone closer to the sound.
The song doesn\'t stay in one key.
Blues, modal tunes and songs full of passing chords can pull it toward a neighboring key.
In Band and Guitar modes the tempo can lock onto double or half the real speed. Tap the BPM number to switch between them. A song in 6/8 or 12/8 often shows as 2/4 or 4/4.
Singing rarely gives a steady beat, so in Voices mode you tap the tempo yourself.
Chords show up a second or two late, because KeyCatch listens a little ahead to be sure.
Rich chords are shown as the nearest simple one. A Cmaj9 might show as Cmaj7 or C.
If your band tunes to something other than A = 440, set it in Settings so \"in tune\" means what you expect.
KeyCatch is new, and we haven\'t tried it in every kind of room or with every kind of band yet.
When it matters, trust your ears. If something looks off, press New song to start fresh.
KeyCatch is published by Rivers Research. © 2026 Rivers Research.

KeyCatch listens with three open research models: CREPE, by Jong Wook Kim, Justin Salamon, Peter Li and Juan Pablo Bello (MIT License), Basic Pitch, by Spotify\'s Audio Intelligence Lab (Apache 2.0), and Beat This!, by Francesco Foscarin, Jan Schlüter and Gerhard Widmer (MIT License). Text is set in Manrope (SIL Open Font License), and the icons are Google\'s Material Symbols (Apache 2.0). Their licenses ship with the app.
Everything happens on your phone. No audio leaves it unless you choose to share a recorded clip yourself.
